promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Principles of training applied to performance

questions.q: In the principles of training, what does 'specificity' mean?
options: Training that is matched to the specific sport, muscles and energy systems used
Gradually increasing the amount you train over time
The loss of fitness when training stops
Training that becomes boring and repetitive
questions.explain: Specificity means training should be relevant and appropriate to the activity, using the correct muscles and energy systems.

questions.q: In the FITT principle, what does the 'I' stand for?
options: Intensity
Individuality
Interval
Improvement
questions.explain: FITT stands for Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type, all of which can be adjusted to apply overload.

questions.q: In the FITT principle, the 'F' refers to which variable?
options: Frequency (how often you train)
Force (how hard you push)
Fatigue (how tired you get)
Flexibility (range of movement)
questions.explain: Frequency describes how often training takes place, for example the number of sessions per week.

questions.q: Which principle describes the loss of fitness that occurs when a performer stops or reduces training?
options: Reversibility
Progressive overload
Specificity
Frequency
questions.explain: Reversibility means fitness gains are lost if training intensity or frequency is reduced or stopped altogether.

questions.q: What does 'progressive overload' involve?
options: Gradually increasing the amount of training so the body adapts safely
Training only the muscles used in the chosen sport
Keeping training exactly the same each week
Reducing training as a competition approaches
questions.explain: Progressive overload means gradually making training harder over time so the body adapts and fitness improves without injury.

questions.q: Why should overload be applied progressively rather than all at once?
options: To allow the body to adapt gradually and reduce the risk of injury
To make training more boring for the performer
To ensure fitness is lost more quickly
To keep the intensity below the training threshold
questions.explain: Increasing training too quickly can cause injury, so overload is added gradually to let the body adapt safely.

questions.q: A sprinter mainly performs short, explosive runs in training rather than long-distance jogs. Which principle does this best demonstrate?
options: Specificity
Reversibility
Tedium
Frequency
questions.explain: Training short explosive runs is specific to the demands and energy systems used in sprinting.

questions.q: A performer returns from a six-week injury and finds their aerobic fitness has dropped noticeably. Which principle explains this?
options: Reversibility
Progressive overload
Specificity
Intensity
questions.explain: A long break from training causes reversibility, where fitness adaptations are gradually lost.

questions.q: A footballer currently trains twice a week and wants to overload using the 'F' of FITT. What should they do?
options: Increase the number of training sessions per week
Lift heavier weights in each session
Make each session last longer
Change from running to swimming
questions.explain: Frequency is overloaded by increasing how often training takes place, for example moving from two to three sessions a week.

questions.q: A netball player already trains hard but wants to overload using the 'I' of FITT. Which change achieves this?
options: Working at a higher heart rate or lifting a heavier load
Adding an extra session on Saturday
Training for five minutes longer each time
Swapping shooting practice for defending practice
questions.explain: Intensity is overloaded by making the performer work harder, such as raising the heart rate or increasing resistance.

questions.q: How is an 'open' skill best described?
options: A skill affected by the environment and performed in unpredictable conditions
A skill performed in a stable, predictable environment
A skill requiring very little thought or concentration
A skill that cannot be improved with practice
questions.explain: Open skills are influenced by the environment and others, so they are often externally paced and unpredictable.

questions.q: Which of these is the best example of a closed skill?
options: A gymnast performing a vault
A footballer dribbling past opponents
A rugby player making a tackle
A tennis player returning a serve
questions.explain: A vault is a closed skill because it is self-paced and performed in a predictable, stable environment.

questions.q: What is a 'basic' (simple) skill?
options: A skill that requires little thought or concentration to perform
A skill that is always performed in an unpredictable environment
A skill that can only be done by elite performers
A skill that involves several difficult movements combined together
questions.explain: Basic skills such as running or jogging require minimal decision-making and concentration.

questions.q: Why is a pass in a hockey match usually classed as an open skill?
options: Because it is affected by opponents and the changing environment around the player
Because it is always performed in exactly the same way
Because it requires no decision-making at all
Because it is never influenced by other players
questions.explain: The pass must be adjusted to opponents, team-mates and the situation, making it an environment-dependent open skill.

questions.q: A tennis serve is often classified as a complex skill. Why?
options: Because it requires a high level of concentration and coordination to perform
Because it needs no practice to master
Because the environment is always unpredictable
Because it can be performed without any technique
questions.explain: Complex skills demand greater attention, judgement and coordination than basic skills.

questions.q: A performer takes a free throw in basketball, in their own time and in a predictable, stationary environment. How is this skill best classified?
options: Closed and self-paced
Open and externally paced
Open and unpredictable
Environment-dependent
questions.explain: A free throw is self-paced and unaffected by a changing environment, making it a closed skill.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of analysing and evaluating performance?
options: To identify strengths and weaknesses in order to plan improvement
To decide the final league position of a team
To measure only how tall a performer is
To replace the need for any training
questions.explain: Analysis and evaluation identify what a performer does well and less well so that targeted improvements can be planned.

questions.q: Within performance analysis, what is meant by a 'strength'?
options: An aspect of performance the performer does well
An aspect of performance that needs improvement
A type of resistance training
A principle of training
questions.explain: A strength is a component or skill the performer executes effectively and consistently.

questions.q: After identifying a weakness in a performer, what is the logical next step in the process?
options: Create an action plan of training to improve that weakness
Ignore it and only train existing strengths
Immediately enter a major competition
Stop all training to allow recovery
questions.explain: Once a weakness is identified, a targeted action plan or training programme is designed to bring about improvement.

questions.q: Why is collecting data (such as timings or shot success rates) useful when evaluating a performance?
options: It provides objective evidence to judge performance and measure improvement
It guarantees the performer will win
It removes the need to watch the performance
It only shows the performer's weaknesses
questions.explain: Objective data allows performance to be measured accurately and compared over time to track improvement.

questions.q: A coach notices a hockey player has excellent passing but poor stamina. Using analysis and evaluation, what should the coach do?
options: Set the stamina as a target and plan continuous training to improve it
Only practise passing because it is already strong
Advise the player to stop training completely
Reclassify passing as a closed skill
questions.explain: The identified weakness (stamina) becomes a training target, addressed with an appropriate method such as continuous training.
